title: Don't Teach Students 'How to Think,' Teach Them What Is True ch_them_what_is_true_1196087.html
author: Kate Bierly
summary: Kate Bierly argues that the popular slogan 'don't teach what to think, teach how to think' is an insufficient defense against ideological indoctrination in schools. She contends the Left has already shaped the 'how' through critical pedagogy rooted in Paulo Freire's critical consciousness framework. The solution, she argues, is disciplined inquiry grounded in primary texts of American history and Western civilization.
points: The slogan 'teach how to think, not what to think' is insufficient because critical pedagogy already controls the how
Critical consciousness, popularized by Paulo Freire, teaches students to interpret society through power and oppression rather than truth
Critical theory conflicts with the Declaration of Independence, which grounds rights in human nature, not social position
A free society requires citizens formed in truths that sustain liberty, not just students trained to evaluate arguments
The solution is disciplined inquiry rooted in primary texts of American history and Western civilization
quotes: Critical thinking teaches students to evaluate evidence, identify logical fallacies, and assess arguments. These are worthwhile skills, but they are reactive.
Popularized by Paulo Freire in Pedagogy of the Oppressed, critical consciousness teaches students to interpret society primarily through relationships of power and oppression.
A free society therefore requires more than students capable of analyzing arguments; it requires citizens formed in the truths that sustain liberty.

Critical pedagogy is already teaching students how to think. It teaches them which questions to ask, which assumptions to examine, and which moral framework to adopt before evidence is ever considered.
This is why the slogan "Don't teach children what to think, teach them how to think" is not a solution — it is a surrender. The Left has already seized the "how.
